9B.1 Anointing (inauguration ceremony) for new civil leader coming into office.

precepts.text: Two are better than one, and if two lie together they have heat, which is exactly what David's servants sought for him.
precepts.point: Abishag the Shunammite is found and ministers to the king, but he does not know her. That means he did not have relations with her; she was there only to keep him warm.

note.label: 1 Kings 1: A King Exalts Himself and a King Is Anointed

precepts.why:
“Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.” “Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone?”

That is exactly what David's servants sought for him. King David “was old and stricken in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he gat no heat.” This is one of the things that happens with age, when the body no longer produces heat as it did in youth and strength. So they sought a young virgin, “and let her lie in thy bosom, that my lord the king may get heat.”

Abishag the Shunammite was found, and she “cherished the king, and ministered to him: but the king knew her not.” That means he did not have relations with her. She was there only to keep him warm.

precepts.text: The Most High chose Judah, then David's house, then Solomon among David's sons to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.
precepts.point: David repeats the oath he swore by the Lord God of Israel, that Solomon his son shall reign after him and sit upon his throne in his stead. The throne belongs to Solomon by that sworn word.

note.label: 1 Kings 1: A King Exalts Himself and a King Is Anointed

precepts.why:
“Howbeit the Lord God of Israel chose me before all the house of my father to be king over Israel for ever: for he hath chosen Judah to be the ruler; and of the house of Judah, the house of my father; and among the sons of my father he liked me to make me king over all Israel: And of all my sons, (for the Lord hath given me many sons,) he hath chosen Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.”

The Most High chose Judah, then David's house, then Solomon among all David's sons. So when David says, “Assuredly Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne in my stead”, he is repeating the oath he swore by the Lord God of Israel. The throne belongs to Solomon by that sworn word.

points: David is old and cannot stay warm, so his servants seek a fair young woman to lie in his bosom and give him heat. This is one of the things that happens with age, when the body no longer produces heat as it did in youth and strength.

note.label: 1 Kings 1: A King Exalts Himself and a King Is Anointed

points: Abishag the Shunammite is found and ministers to the king, but he does not know her. That means he did not have relations with her; she was there only to keep him warm.

note.label: 1 Kings 1: A King Exalts Himself and a King Is Anointed

points: Adonijah exalts himself, saying he will be king, and prepares chariots and horsemen to promote himself. He takes the throne to himself rather than receiving it from the Most High.

note.label: 1 Kings 1: A King Exalts Himself and a King Is Anointed

points: David repeats the oath he swore by the Lord God of Israel, that Solomon his son shall reign after him and sit upon his throne in his stead. The throne belongs to Solomon by that sworn word.

note.label: 1 Kings 1: A King Exalts Himself and a King Is Anointed

points: David commands that Solomon be set on the king's own mule and brought to Gihon, where Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him king over Israel. The people come up rejoicing so that the earth rings with the sound.
